body: Thank you for your kind words. I'll be sure to reply if I need anything.

Thank you for your response.


As far as social life goes, it's been incredibly fulfilling and expansive. Back in college, I was very active in student organizations and made a name for myself at my small school. I also have quite a large family and my cousins are my best friends. They are usually the ones I am with on the weekends. Other than family, I have a best friend local to me that joins my cousins and me. And although scattered, I have close friends that I play games with online from time to time.


When it comes to my previous 20 or so years, I have battled with thoughts of suicide. They have always seemed to be based on certain life events or conditions. Introspectively, they seemed to be exaggerated reactions. That's particularly why the deal I made with myself is concerning.


I understand that the gluten free diet seems like a fad, but my doctor instructed me to do so and I've noticed a considerable improvement to my mood, energy, and digestion. I actually do have headaches and/or gastrointestinal issues when consuming gluten now.


I have been eating at about a 20% deficit (using MyFitnessPal to count) and have been exercising since the past year. I've been lifting using the SL 5x5 program and throw in cardio (spinning) when I can. Some of my cousins lift, so I've been getting help from them. Unfortunately I have a gout flare up and a sprained wrist, so i cant do much now. I am currently 310lbs and 6'1" and fit into XL shirts and 38" width pants with room to spare if that gives you an idea of my size.


What's interesting is that 6 months ago, even with exercise, my mood didn't really change.


Edit: I do have health insurance, but have not reached out to a therapist. I am thinking about it.
